inconsistencies: #34038 and #35387 solve the same problem (trace logging unusable without paired -debug, no runtime control). Review #34038 first: it is the broader change and #35355 is built on it; #35387 should be closed or rebased on whichever approach wins.

HTTP framing chain from the libevent removal (#35182): #36652 (requests executing after a closing reply), #36643 (Transfer-Encoding validation) and #36642 (batch id reset) touch the same request-parsing path. Order matters: #36652 first, then #36643, then #36642.
#36124 rewrites HTTPRequest state handling and will conflict with #36652, #36643 and #36259; land the behavioural fixes before the encapsulation refactor.

#36384 (self.Arg<> across node and wallet RPCs) likely subsumes #34950 (self.Arg<> for generatetoaddress). Check overlap and review #36384 first. #36167 also refactors RPC argument helpers and overlaps both.
#36503 (crash on assumeutxo rollback without tip data) and #36266 (early failure plus concurrency guard for dumptxoutset) harden the same RPC; review #36503 first since it fixes a crash.

PSBT cluster touching overlapping code: #36343 (finalize verification), #36567 (stale taproot/musig signatures), #36569 (analyzepsbt negative fee), #36332 (musig2 data leakage), #35370 (key-origin modes), #36382 (control block warnings). #36343 is the correctness anchor and should go first.
#35728 and #36002 both change node::GetTransaction error semantics (throwing on I/O errors vs. returning candidate block hashes for pruned blocks). Reconcile the error contract; review #35728 first.

Assumeutxo surface is touched by #33117, #36503, #36220 and #35054; #33117's RPC refactor changes loadtxoutset failure codes to internal errors, which should be checked against #36503's new error paths.
result.notes: The category is dominated by one theme: correctness of the internal HTTP server after the libevent replacement (#36187, #36652, #36643, #36642, #36259, #36204, #36200, #36124). Those plus the endpoints returning wrong or silently incomplete data (#35837, #36385, #35728) are where review attention belongs. Feature additions were kept at P2 only where an external consumer or long-standing issue is cited; diagnostic or convenience additions without a named consumer sit in mid-to-low P3.
